blocks.explanation:
A fraction of sums of sines and cosines must reduce to \(\tan\alpha\).
Expand all four terms: half of them cancel.
Plan: expand top, expand bottom, cancel the common factor.
steps:
Given: the statement.
To show: the fraction equals \(\tan\alpha\).
Method: \(\sin(\alpha \pm \beta)\) and \(\cos(\alpha \pm \beta)\) formulas.

Expand the numerator
\[\sin(\alpha + \beta) + \sin(\alpha - \beta)\]
\[= (\sin\alpha\cos\beta + \cos\alpha\sin\beta)\]
\[+ (\sin\alpha\cos\beta - \cos\alpha\sin\beta)\]
\[= 2\sin\alpha\cos\beta\]
Why: The \(\cos\alpha\sin\beta\) terms cancel.

Expand the denominator
\[\cos(\alpha + \beta) + \cos(\alpha - \beta)\]
\[= (\cos\alpha\cos\beta - \sin\alpha\sin\beta)\]
\[+ (\cos\alpha\cos\beta + \sin\alpha\sin\beta)\]
\[= 2\cos\alpha\cos\beta\]
Why: The \(\sin\alpha\sin\beta\) terms cancel.

Divide
\[\text{L.H.S.} = \dfrac{2\sin\alpha\cos\beta}{2\cos\alpha\cos\beta}\]
\[= \dfrac{\sin\alpha}{\cos\alpha} = \tan\alpha = \text{R.H.S.}\]
Why: \(2\cos\beta\) is common to top and bottom (\(\cos\beta \ne 0\)).

Check with \(\alpha = 45^{\circ}\), \(\beta = 45^{\circ}\)
\[\dfrac{\sin 90^{\circ} + \sin 0^{\circ}}{\cos 90^{\circ} + \cos 0^{\circ}} = \dfrac{1}{1} = 1\]
\[\tan 45^{\circ} = 1 \;\checkmark\]
Why: A quick test agrees.
